newsitem.title: POLAND: Universal bids for Polish news-stands-PAP.
newsitem.headline: Universal bids for Polish news-stands-PAP.

text.p: Trading firm Universal SA has bid to buy up to 51-percent stake in Polish state-owned news-stand chain Ruch SA to rival French Hachette, PAP news agency quoted the privatisation minister as saying on Wednesday.

PAP quoted Wieslaw Kaczmarek as saying that Universal's investment bid, on Tuesday, was the same as that of a Polish consortium, which earlier offered to buy the a 51-percent stake in Ruch for $120 million or 40 percent for $80 million.
"Universal sent the privatisation ministry its own offer for buying Ruch," PAP quoted Kaczmarek as saying.
The two offers are outside the official tender for Ruch, in which Hachette -- leading of a consortium of Polish investors -- remains the only bidder.
Hachette wants to buy a controlling stake in Ruch but other details of its offer have not been disclosed.
Kaczmarek can annul the tender and open a new one but so far he has said he plans to continue negotiations with Hachette.
On Tuesday he said he expected the French company to present a final written investment offer this week to allow him to decide whether to sell it Ruch.
Ruch, controlling 65 percent of the press distribution market with 17,000 kiosks nationwide, netted 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995.
